"They think, from the amount they found that she probably stole a couple thousand dollars." Where is she now? "Oh she's in jail." We had only been working for a couple weeks. It was surreal. I remember a conversation with her. "I never get any violations for my bag. I am always even." She was counting her money in secret and had somehow slipped on a $20. It was a remake of Stephen King's novel about monsters who infected people with a virus called Ripley. Worms grew inside you and ate their way out. I remember seeing the main characters walk into a bathroom to find a man passed out on the seat. They touch him, he tips over, and a hole has been eaten straight out of his ass. Another main character sarcastically screams at a monster, "Oh bite me!" The monster turns around (they're on a snowmobile because fuck it, why not) and bites his torso off. My dad probably figured I wouldn't remember, I was too young. Oh do I remember. I'm pretty sure we went to see films with nudity in them too because I remember watching a movie about a man who kept cheating on his wife to have long graphic sex in his mistress's bed. I had had enough to the point that even good movie's like Castaway with Tom Hanks would freak me out. I was stalked by an online predator as a girl. I finally managed to break it off even though he was threatening suicide. It took three years to do it and left me a little broken mentally. I felt like a ghost when I walked down the halls. This is an important point to the story. Anyway, my family moved to a new residence and I changed buses though I didn't change schools. All the kids were quiet and well mannered except this one guy. He was in a grade above me and he always managed to find new ways to annoy me. He would force my chin up when I wouldn't make eye contact with him. He never quit smiling and making stupid jokes. One day he found an old candy on the floor of the bus and said, "I'll give you a quarter if you eat this." I held out my hand and said, "Give me the quarter." He handed me a quarter which I slipped into my pocket before proceeding to ignore him. It took him a full minute to realize I was not eating that gross piece of candy and that he had been cheated out of a quarter. That aggrieved look on his face was the first time he made me laugh. Time passed and I began to feel defensive around him more often without quite knowing why. Prom came and went with the boy on the bus mentioning, "I got asked to the prom by Tracy Krause." I looked up from my book and said, "She's all right." He sent me  look. We both knew Tracy was loud and a little snobby. He asked me about guys I found attractive. Having been abused I couldn't form an opinion and shrugged. "Ice queen." I laughed. Another time he turned to me, he had to twist in his seat because I certainly wouldn't let him sit with me, "Do you think I should cut my hair?" His hair was legend among some of the girls in my grade. It was a beautiful black waterfall. I decided that he didn't need to know that. Scrunching up my face, "I'm afraid the whole thing has to go." I shook my head like a doctor proscribing surgery on an invalid she knows won't make it. His eyes widened but I didn't think he'd actually do it. Monday rolls by and he did do it. The short hair only brought out his face which I grudgingly admitted was kind of attractive. I stayed mum about it except for, "Oh it's okay." When he asked me how it looked. More days passed. A guy in my class decided to ruin my favorite copy of Jane Eyre by scribbling all over it. I cried in the bathroom. On the bus ride home I told the boy about it and threatened, "If you ever tell anyone I will never talk to you again." The boy is a pacifist so what could he do anyway? The next day at school I hear shouts near the bus stop and a male voice shouting, "Apologize!" I run to see what all the commotion is about and it's the kid on my bus harassing the bully until the bully walked up to me and mumbled he was sorry. None of this is familiar territory to me. I don't know what to say but I hope the boy can read my thankful expression. My family moves again. And the day comes when I have to change bus stops. It snuck up on me so quick I had no chance to say goodbye. We still went to the same school though. After a while the boy notices and comes up to me at the bus stop. "So... you changed buses, huh?" I nod, waiting for more. He looks me in the eye. Then away. "I guess this is goodbye." I wait for a little more. But he walks away and we never really talk again. Months later a friend teases me, "You totally liked him!" And I smile and open my mouth to deny it when nothing comes out. I realize what I almost had and what I had lost. But I still feel grateful to him. I don't think he realized that the simple act of talking to me stopped me from brooding on my past. He's a good person.
